text: Intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) is a life-threatening medical condition that indicates bleeding within the skull. The compression of blood in the brain can lead to other causes of serious complications and death if proper treatment has not been taken promptly. ICH has five categories: Intraventricular (IVH), Intraparenchymal (IPH), Subarachnoid (SAH), Epidural (EDH), and Subdural (SDH); where each has different causes, symptoms, and treatments[ 1 ]. Multiple bleeding location, as well as cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and gray/white matters, are essential for managing hemorrhage and treatment plan [ 2 , 3 ].
